item.title: AI Gateway - Route across a pool of models with model aliases
item.description:
AI Gateway now supports model aliases. A model alias is a pool of models that your application calls by one name, such as custom/support-fast. AI Gateway tries the models in the order you set and falls back to the next one if a request fails, or uses smart routing to choose a model for each request.

Because your application only references the alias, you can swap models or change the routing algorithm on your gateway without redeploying. Create and manage aliases on your gateway's Routing page, alongside dynamic routes.

To call an alias through the REST API, use its name as the model. For example, send this body to /accounts/{account_id}/ai/run:

Include the cf-aig-gateway-id header to select the gateway where you created the alias. Aliases are scoped to individual gateways.

For setup instructions and routing options, refer to Model aliases.

item.title: Bots - Granular access controls for the top Personal Agents
item.description:
The Configure AI bot policies setting is now named AI Crawler and Agent access policies.

Personal agents act on a person's behalf, fetching information or browsing in response to a request. The updated policies let you set actions for the top Personal Agents individually. This gives you control over agent access while allowing visitors to use agents to find answers or compare products using your site's content.

Customize how Personal Agents access your site via Security > Settings > AI Crawler and Agent access policies.

For more information, check out our blog ↗︎ or refer to our documentation for AI Crawler and Agent access policies.

item.title: Browser Isolation, Cloudflare One - Block data entry with Browser Isolation without losing search, copy, and zoom (beta)
item.description:
Isolation policies now support a third keyboard option in beta: Allow read-only actions. Previously, the keyboard setting was binary — allow all input or block everything. With Allow read-only actions, you can block data entry while preserving the built-in browser actions your users depend on.

In Allow read-only actions mode, users can still find in page, select all, copy, print, and zoom. All other keyboard input is blocked from reaching the isolated page. Copy and print remain subject to their own policy settings, so the controls compose instead of overriding each other. For example, setting the keyboard to Allow read-only actions and copy to Do not allow lets users search and zoom but prevents them from copying content.

To use this feature, set Keyboard to Allow read-only actions in your isolation policy settings. Via the API, set keyboard to enable_read_only_actions in the biso_admin_controls object with version set to v2.

For more information, refer to Keyboard.

item.title: Cloudflare Network Firewall - New managed rule to help mitigate CVE-2026-98432.
item.description:
Cloudflare Network Firewall has a new managed rule to help mitigate the Linux IPv4 TCP use-after-free vulnerability (CVE-2026-98432 ↗︎):

  • Rule name: Block CVE-2026-98432 ↗︎ traffic
  • Rule ID: 6a4df2bf984946a88c74b07349557e83

The rule is disabled by default. To use it:

  1. Go to Networking > Firewall Policies > Managed Rulesets.
  2. Enable the rule with action Log first.
  3. Review traffic that matches the rule.
  4. If the matching traffic is not expected for your environment, change the action to Block.

For more information on enabling managed rulesets, refer to Enable managed rulesets.

For more details about the vulnerability, including an agent assessment prompt and evidence sources, refer to the Cloudflare Radar Zero Wire briefing ↗︎.

item.title: Load Balancing, Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare Mesh - Steer Cloudflare One users and private networks to the same endpoint with session affinity and hash steering in private load balancers
item.description:
Private load balancers can now keep each user on the same endpoint. This helps with applications that keep session state on a single server.

Two options are available:

  • Hash endpoint steering. In the dashboard, set a pool's Endpoint steering to Hash. Each user is mapped to an endpoint within the pool.
  • Session affinity. With the API, set session_affinity to ip_cookie on the load balancer. Each user stays on the same endpoint while it remains healthy and your pools do not change. Refer to Session affinity.

For traffic from the Cloudflare One Client, Cloudflare identifies the user by their device, so a user stays on the same endpoint even if their IP address changes. For other traffic, such as from a Cloudflare WAN site, Cloudflare uses the source IP address.

This works for endpoints reached through Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare Mesh, and Cloudflare WAN. Affinity pins the endpoint, not the cloudflared or Mesh replica that carries the traffic.

To learn how private load balancing fits with your connectors, refer to Load balance private network traffic.

item.title: Workers - Count weighted requests with the Rate Limiting binding API in Workers
item.description:
Requests can require different amounts of work. A product lookup might be cheap, while a search runs an expensive database query. Use weighted requests to make expensive operations consume more of the same rate limit.

The Rate Limiting binding now accepts an optional delta in limit(). Pass delta to choose how many units a call consumes.

For example, assign one unit to a product lookup and 10 units to an expensive search. Both operations consume the same user's allowance. The following handler takes a verified user ID from your application's authentication flow:

The delta defaults to 1. To use delta in local development, use Wrangler 4.157.0 ↗︎ or later. For TypeScript support, use @cloudflare/workers-types version 5.20261106.1 or later.

For more details, refer to Weighted requests.

item.title: Cloudflare One Client - Cloudflare One Client for Linux (version 2026.7.1385.0)
item.description:
A new GA release for the Linux Cloudflare One Client is now available on the stable releases downloads page.

This hotfix addresses an issue building trusted certificate chains.

item.title: Agents - Agents SDK now supports Pi 1.5 with fewer storage writes and lower memory use
item.description:
Agents SDK v0.33.0 upgrades PiHarness to Pi 1.5 ↗︎. The release reduces storage transactions while streaming, improves throughput across many sessions, and reduces memory use when streaming large tool calls.

Performance improvements

  • Far fewer storage writes while streaming. Pi stores streamed answers and tool output in batches, within a second of each update, instead of on every update. Over SQLite, this cuts storage transactions by about 27x for long answers and 5.7x for turns with parallel tools, and CPU by about a quarter.
  • Higher throughput across many sessions. Pi's scheduler no longer rechecks every conversation on each commit. In a SQLite benchmark with 2,048 sessions, one Pi harness went from 88 to 459 agent runs per second.
  • Less memory on large answers. Streaming a 500 KB tool call used to take about 20 seconds of CPU and a 100 MB heap. Pi now appends new text instead of copying it on every update.

Streaming updates remain visible immediately, but are persisted in batches. With the default settings, a crash can lose up to about one second of streamed progress. Refer to Recovery to configure this interval.

Session and tool updates

  • A view of each session. session.watch() replaces session.events(). It returns the newest transcript entries and the session's live state, such as the answer being streamed, running tools, and why the last run ended without an answer.
  • Continue without adding a message. The new session.continue() API starts a new run using the existing transcript, for example after a model error or when a run reaches its turn limit.
  • Turn limit. defaults.maxTurns caps the tool rounds a run can take in new sessions.
  • Tasks that keep crashing end. Pi now ends a task cut off by its restart limit instead of parking it. retry() and the parked status are removed.
  • Browser in Pi's code mode. Scripts in Pi's code mode can call browserTool and pass its screenshots to image(). browserTool also stops when the harness aborts its call.

Continue an unanswered conversation

For an existing session and submission operationId, check the result before offering a continuation. For example, after resolving a model error:

This starts a new run without appending a user message. The session must be idle. If the transcript already ends in an answer, the operation returns unanswered with reason nothing_to_answer. Refer to Work with sessions.

Upgrade

Once a conversation runs on Pi 1.5, Pi 1.4 cannot read it. After upgrading, roll forward to fix deployment issues rather than rolling back to Pi 1.4.

Update callers of session.events() to use session.watch(), and remove uses of retry() and the parked status. Refer to the Pi Durable 1.5.0 changelog ↗︎ for the full list of breaking changes.

The Agents SDK v0.33.0 changelog ↗︎ has step-by-step upgrade instructions. Point your coding agent at them and upgrade today:

item.title: AI Gateway - New AI Gateways require authentication
item.description:
New AI Gateways now require authentication to prevent unauthorized requests. Once authentication is on, you cannot turn it off through the dashboard or API.

When you create a new AI Gateway through the API, authentication is on by default. You can leave out the authentication field or set it to true. If you set it to false, the API returns HTTP 400.

When you update an existing gateway, leaving out authentication keeps its current setting. If you try to turn off authentication after it is on, the API returns HTTP 400.

Existing gateways with authentication turned off can continue without it. You can turn it on in your gateway settings or include authentication: true in a gateway update request:

Before turning authentication on, configure HTTP clients to send a valid Cloudflare API token. Requests through Workers bindings remain pre-authenticated.

For setup instructions and supported authorization headers, refer to AI Gateway authentication.

item.title: Bots - See which AI assistants act for your users in Account Abuse Protection
item.description:
Account Abuse Protection now shows when a recognized AI assistant makes a login or sign up request, and which account it was acting for.

  • Population overview: See which AI assistants are active across your users and how many accounts use them.
  • Account activity: Every login and sign up event shows whether an AI assistant made the request, and which one.
  • AI assistant filters: filter accounts by number of AI assistant events or number of AI assistants.

Use this to investigate and mitigate a single account without blocking an assistant for everyone else who relies on it, and to tune your agent settings in AI Crawler and Agent access policies.

AI assistant visibility covers login and sign up events only. Requests from assistants that Cloudflare does not recognize appear as ordinary traffic.

For more information, refer to AI assistants.

item.title: Browser Run - Crawl results include URL outcomes and robots.txt diagnostics
item.description:
Browser Run /crawl results now include more detailed diagnostics. Each URL record can include an outcome that identifies the specific processing result, such as success, robots_disallowed, timeout, or page_error.

The job-level robots array reports the robots.txt state for up to 50 origins encountered by the crawl. Each entry includes the origin, whether usable rules were available, and the HTTP status when the crawler received a response.

For field definitions and all possible outcome values, refer to URL outcomes and robots.txt diagnostics.

item.title: R2 - Request metrics breakdown by region and HTTP error code
item.description:
You can now compare regional activity and errors by HTTP status code on the Metrics page for a R2 bucket in the Cloudflare dashboard.

Go to Bucket metrics ↗

Compare regions

Use Request Distribution by Region to compare request activity and filter by writes, reads, errors, or rate-limited errors (429).

Inspect errors

Use Errors by Status Code to compare error counts and trends.

To troubleshoot errors, refer to the R2 error code reference.

item.title: Radar - Zero Wire, a hub for investigating critical Internet vulnerabilities
item.description:
Cloudflare Radar now includes Zero Wire ↗︎, a hub for investigating critical Internet vulnerabilities and threats. Each briefing separates confirmed facts from open questions, lists remediation steps, and shows what Cloudflare observes about the threat.

Briefings

Briefings are grouped by urgency. Needs attention covers active incidents, new guidance, or unresolved scope that security teams should review now. Reference keeps stable briefings available, even if not every affected system has been patched. Each card shows the recommended action and summarizes what happened, why it matters, and what to do.

Each briefing page expands on the card with an update chronology and an overview, followed by:

  • What to do now: remediation steps, plus a prompt to copy into an AI agent with access to your infrastructure, asking for an evidence-based assessment of affected systems and exposure.
  • Cloudflare coverage: the Cloudflare products that protect against the threat, and any impact on Cloudflare's own services.
  • Evidence and sources: vendor advisories, CVE records, the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, and Radar charts, such as requests matching the related Cloudflare WAF rules.

Follow updates

Search briefings by CVE, name, or tag, or browse every briefing with a given tag. To follow new briefings and updates, subscribe to the Zero Wire RSS feed ↗︎ or to the feed of a single tag. New briefings also appear in the Caught on Radar ↗︎ section of the Radar homepage.

Send questions or feedback from any briefing page, or at radar@cloudflare.com.

For more details, read the blog post ↗︎ or visit Zero Wire ↗︎.

item.title: WAF - WAF Release - 2026-11-03
item.description:
This release introduces updates to the underlying rule expressions for PHP out-of-memory (OOM) vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 ↗︎, CVE-2026-109619 ↗︎ and CVE-2026-115560 ↗︎. The improvements are iterative changes based on reports from Security Researchers as part of PHP Capture the Flag (CTF) challenge ↗︎.

item.title: AI Search - AI Search billing postponed to December 1, 2026, and default sync interval is now 24 hours
item.description:
Billing postponed to December 1, 2026

AI Search billing has been postponed by one month and now begins on December 1, 2026, instead of November 1, 2026. You will not be charged for AI Search usage before December 1, 2026. Pricing and included usage are unchanged.

For rates and included usage, refer to Limits & pricing.

Default sync interval is now 24 hours

The default sync interval for AI Search instances is changing from 6 hours to 24 hours. You can still choose any supported interval, from 15 minutes to 24 hours, with the Sync interval setting in your instance settings or the sync_interval field in the API.

For details, refer to Sync interval.

item.title: Bots - New Account Abuse Protection Dashboard
item.description:
Account Abuse Protection customers in Early Access can now investigate login and sign up activity in a dedicated dashboard under Security > Account Abuse Protection.

  • Population overview: See total login and sign up events, unique accounts, IPs and devices, top countries and ASNs, and leaked credential check results. Filter accounts by signals such as leaked credential events and unique IPs to find the accounts that need review.
  • Individual Account overview: Review a single Hashed User ID's activity, including its top networks, locations and devices, and an event log with the Ray ID for each event. Mitigate the account with a Security Rule on its Hashed User ID.
  • New roles: The Account Abuse Protection role grants access to the dashboard. Account Abuse Protection PII role grants access to the dashboard as well as account-level PII, such as email address, and is required to create or edit Logpush jobs that include PII. The dashboard includes all login and sign up events from the date the feature was enabled.

For more information, refer to Account Abuse Protection.

item.title: Cloudflare One, Access - Organize and authorize Access service tokens with tags
item.description:
You can now assign key-value tags to Access service tokens and use those tags to organize credentials or control application access. Each token supports up to five tags, such as environment: production or team: payments.

Add or edit tags when you create or update a token in the dashboard or service token API. You can search and filter by tag on the Service Tokens page. Tags also appear in Resource Tagging, where you can query them alongside other tagged resources.

The Service Token Tag policy selector matches valid tokens with an exact key-value pair. Use it in a Service Auth policy to authorize tokens by environment or team without listing each token individually. For example, this API policy configuration accepts valid tokens tagged environment: production:

For setup instructions, refer to Tag service tokens and Authorize service tokens by tag.

item.title: Flagship - Evaluate Flagship flags locally
item.description:
Flagship bindings now evaluate flags against a local flag store during local development, instead of calling your remote app. You can develop offline and test flag changes without affecting production. This applies to wrangler dev, the Cloudflare Vite plugin, the Vitest integration, and cf dev.

The local store starts empty, so evaluations return the default value you pass in code. Add and manage local flags in any of these ways:

  • Wrangler — Add --local to wrangler flagship flags commands, such as create, update, and evaluate. To copy all flags from your remote app, run npx wrangler flagship flags pull <APP_ID>.
  • Local Explorer — Create, edit, toggle, and evaluate flags in Local Explorer while your dev server runs.
  • cf CLI — Add --local to cf flagship commands.

To keep evaluating against your remote app instead, set remote: true on the binding.

The local flag store requires Wrangler v4.135.0 or @cloudflare/vite-plugin v1.56.0 or later. Flagship in Local Explorer requires Wrangler v4.148.0 or @cloudflare/vite-plugin v1.63.0 or later.

Refer to Flagship local development for details.

item.title: Workers - Workers will use the new module registry by default on November 17
item.description:
Starting November 17, 2026, JavaScript Workers with a compatibility date of 2026-11-17 or later will use the new module registry by default. You will no longer need the new_module_registry flag for these dates. Python Workers keep using the legacy registry.

The module registry finds and loads JavaScript modules in your Worker. We announced the new registry in September 2026 ↗︎. It improves compatibility with JavaScript standards and Node.js. In Workers using Node.js compatibility, you can use require() to load ES modules. The module and its dependencies must not use top-level await.

You can also use import.meta to get information about the current module and find the URL of another module without loading it:

When deployed with src/index.ts as the unbundled entrypoint, isEntrypoint is true. helperUrl is a URL within your Worker bundle. Resolving the URL does not check whether the module exists or load it over the network. Build tools may transform import.meta. To try this example directly, refer to unbundled deployments.

Existing Workers keep their current behavior until you change their compatibility date or flags. To try the new registry before November 17, keep your current date and add new_module_registry to your compatibility flags.

Before updating, check your dependencies for invalid import attributes and changes to require() behavior. The new registry rejects invalid import attributes. Calls to require() also fail if the module or any of its dependencies use top-level await. To keep the legacy registry with a compatibility date of 2026-11-17 or later, add legacy_module_registry.

For migration details, refer to the new module registry compatibility flag, bundling documentation, and Node.js compatibility documentation.

item.title: Workers - Request.signal will be enabled by default in Workers on November 17
item.description:
Starting November 17, 2026, Workers with a compatibility date of 2026-11-17 or later will receive client disconnection events through request.signal by default. Use these events to stop unnecessary work when a client leaves. You will no longer need the enable_request_signal compatibility flag for these dates.

We introduced this feature in May 2025. You can log cancellations, clean up resources, or cancel operations that accept an AbortSignal.

For example, this Worker logs a client disconnection and cancels an outgoing request:

Existing Workers keep their current behavior until you change their compatibility date or flags. To try this feature before November 17, keep your current date and add enable_request_signal to your compatibility flags.

With a compatibility date of 2026-11-17 or later, add disable_request_signal to opt out. This change does not enable request_signal_passthrough. Pass the signal explicitly, as the example does.

For more information, refer to the Request API and the Request.signal compatibility flag.

item.title: Cloudflare One, Access - Inspect provisioned users and groups with the SCIM population viewer
item.description:
The SCIM population viewer lets you inspect the users and groups provisioned to Cloudflare One by each identity provider. You can check which resources Cloudflare has received without making API requests or opening a support ticket.

In Zero Trust > Integrations > Identity providers, select a user or group count in SCIM resources to open the viewer. You can:

  • Search users by username, email, name, or resource ID, and groups by name or resource ID.
  • Inspect resource attributes in formatted or JSON views.
  • View group members and compare Cloudflare and IdP resource IDs with provisioning logs.
  • Delete individual resources from the Cloudflare SCIM population when you have edit permission.

The viewer shows provisioned resources rather than provisioning event history. Use SCIM provisioning logs to investigate failed requests. Existing SCIM deprovisioning and policy behavior remain unchanged.

For dashboard instructions and API examples, refer to View SCIM users and groups.

item.title: Audit Logs - Audit Logs v2: Account analytics
item.description:
Audit Logs v2 now includes analytics for account-level audit logs in the Cloudflare dashboard. The Actions over time chart separates successful and failed actions for the selected time range.

Summary cards show Total actions, Unique actors, Products impacted, and Failure rate. Select a card to investigate action types, authentication methods, top actors, top products, or failed actions. You can apply or exclude values as filters to update both the analytics and audit log table.

Account analytics are not available for organization-level audit logs.

For more information, refer to the account analytics documentation.

item.title: Browser Run - Browser Run now runs Chrome 152
item.description:
Browser Run now runs Chrome 152 by default. Your sessions get current web platform features, rendering fixes, and security patches. You do not need to change your code.

This release also includes the following improvements:

  • Updated default User-Agent. The default User-Agent for Quick Actions now reports Chrome 152 instead of Chrome 119. If you allowlist or match the Browser Run User-Agent, update your rules. You can still set your own value with the userAgent parameter. Refer to Automatic request headers.
  • Better site compatibility. Quick Actions requests now look more like requests from a regular Chrome browser, so fewer sites block them.
  • Large response headers. Pages that return large response headers now load correctly.
  • Updated root certificates. Browser Run removed distrusted root certificates from its trust store.
  • Absolute links. /links now returns absolute URLs, and links-only crawls now follow relative links.
  • Better Markdown output. /markdown and crawl Markdown output now keep code block languages.
  • Clearer errors. Quick Actions that time out now return a consistent error. Outbound Workers that throw an exception now return an HTTP error to the browser.

For more information, refer to the Browser Run documentation.

item.title: D1 - D1 will enforce a maximum query result size of 50 MB
item.description:
Beginning Wednesday, November 4, 2026, D1 will enforce a maximum query result size of 50 MB. Queries that return a result larger than 50 MB will fail and return the following error:

The 50 MB limit covers the 99.999th percentile of requests across D1, so most D1 users will not be impacted.

Import and export operations via the REST API are not subject to this limit and will continue to work as they do today.

If your queries return large results, reduce the result size before the enforcement date. For example, select only the columns you need instead of using SELECT *, and paginate large result sets with LIMIT and OFFSET.

For more information, refer to D1 limits and the D1 error list.

item.title: Data Localization Suite, Cloudflare WAN, Cloudflare One - Cloudflare WAN supports regional Gateway HTTP inspection
item.description:
Cloudflare WAN traffic can now use a Gateway processing region with Regional Services. HTTPS traffic enters a Cloudflare data center (that may be outside the selected region) via an IPsec or GRE tunnel, or through Direct CNI, and remains encrypted until Gateway forwards it to the selected region for TLS decryption and HTTP inspection. This feature gives organizations control over where their sensitive traffic is processed, supporting their data sovereignty goals.

This feature requires unified routing. The processing region applies to Gateway HTTP traffic and does not apply to Gateway DNS or network policy processing.

Contact your account team to configure a processing region. For supported regions, configuration details, and limitations, refer to Data residency for Cloudflare One.

item.title: DNS - New DNS records experience is now the default for everyone
item.description:
The new DNS records experience announced in May is now the default for all users on all plans, including Enterprise. The classic DNS records page has been retired and is no longer available in the Cloudflare dashboard.

Changing a record's type

When the new experience first launched, it did not support changing the type of an existing DNS record. Based on your feedback, we have since added this, so you can now change a record's type (for example, from A to CNAME) directly from the DNS records page. Under the hood, the dashboard uses the batch DNS records endpoint for this.

Questions or feedback

If you run into an issue with the new experience, contact your account team or Cloudflare Support.

item.title: DNS - Cloudflare Services for Private Origins is generally available
item.description: Cloudflare Services for Private Origins is generally available. Proxy public hostnames to origins in your private network over Cloudflare WAN, Cloudflare Tunnel, or Cloudflare Mesh. Refer to Private origins and the announcement blog post ↗︎.

item.title: Durable Objects, Workers - Durable Objects now defer code updates by default
item.description:
Durable Objects can stay active across requests, allowing you to run long-running agents, maintain long-lived WebSocket connections and coordinate state across many clients. This is possible because each Durable Object is globally unique, and this means it must run only one version of your code at a time. Previously, when you deployed a change to your Durable Objects code, that change would be applied immediately, which could interrupt in-flight work and terminate open connections.

Durable Objects now defer code updates by default. When you deploy, an active Durable Object can keep running its current code for up to 5 minutes (300 seconds) while it waits to hibernate. This gives in-flight work time to finish. WebSocket connections that use the Hibernation API remain connected when an object adopts new code after hibernating.

For an active Durable Object, a code update follows this flow:

flowchart TD
    accTitle: Code updates for an active Durable Object
    accDescr: By default, an active object can keep running its current code until it hibernates or the delay ends. After hibernating, it starts on new code on the next request. If the delay ends first, or immediate mode is selected, it resets and adopts the new code. Deferral is best effort.
    A["You deploy new code"] -->|"Default: deferred"| B["The object can keep running<br/>its current code"]
    B --> C{"Hibernates before<br/>the delay ends?"}
    C -->|Yes| D["Starts on the new code<br/>on the next request"]
    C -->|No| E["The object resets<br/>and adopts the new code"]
    A -.->|"Override: immediate"| E

To change the delay, add code_update_strategy to durable_objects in your Wrangler configuration:

max_delay is in seconds, from 0 to 86400 (24 hours), with millisecond precision. Omit it to use the default of 300 seconds.

To set the strategy for a single deployment, pass --durable-objects-code-update-mode with immediate or deferred <duration>. For example, apply an update right away during an incident, or when your deployment tooling calls a Durable Object right after deploying and needs the new code:

npx wrangler versions deploy <VERSION_ID>@100% --durable-objects-code-update-mode immediate
yarn wrangler versions deploy <VERSION_ID>@100% --durable-objects-code-update-mode immediate
pnpm wrangler versions deploy <VERSION_ID>@100% --durable-objects-code-update-mode immediate

A deferred code update is best effort and does not guarantee that every operation finishes. The object can still reset before max_delay is reached, for example during a Cloudflare runtime update.

For more information, including how this interacts with gradual deployments and the REST API, refer to Durable Objects code updates.

item.title: SSL/TLS - Keyless SSL supports TLS 1.3 with ECDSA certificates
item.description:
Keyless SSL supports TLS 1.3 for ECDSA certificates. When TLS 1.3 is enabled on your zone, visitors connecting to a hostname that serves a Keyless ECDSA certificate negotiate TLS 1.3, and your private keys stay on your own key server.

Keyless SSL connections that use RSA certificates continue to negotiate up to TLS 1.2.

For details, refer to the Keyless SSL limitations.

item.title: WAF - WAF Release - 2026-10-30 - Emergency
item.description:
This emergency release adds a new rule to the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset, disabled by default, for a vulnerability in Nuxt Image and IPX. The rule offers partial coverage. Please follow the advisory and patch to the latest version.

RulesetRule IDLegacy Rule IDDescriptionPrevious ActionNew ActionComments
Cloudflare Managed RulesetN/ANuxt Image / IPX - Explicit GIF or Animation Modifier ExposureN/ADisabledThis is a new detection.

item.title: WAF - WAF Release - 2026-10-30
item.description:
This release introduces updates to the underlying rule expressions for PHP out-of-memory (OOM) vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 ↗︎, CVE-2026-109619 ↗︎ and CVE-2026-115560 ↗︎. The improvements are iterative changes based on reports from Security Researchers as part of PHP Capture the Flag (CTF) challenge ↗︎.

Cloudflare Free RulesetN/APHP Remote Code Execution Attack (CVE-2026-109618 ↗︎, CVE-2026-109619 ↗︎) #3BlockBlockRule detection updated.
Cloudflare Free RulesetN/APHP Remote Code Execution Attack (CVE-2026-109618 ↗︎, CVE-2026-109619 ↗︎) #4BlockBlockRule detection updated.
Cloudflare Managed RulesetN/APHP Remote Code Execution Attack (CVE-2026-109618 ↗︎, CVE-2026-109619 ↗︎) #3BlockBlockRule detection updated.

Cloudflare Response RulesetN/ADefault block for High confidence SignaturesBlockBlockRule detection updated.

item.title: Workers, BYOIP, Bots - Workers subrequests now preserve context for BYOIP destinations
item.description:
Cloudflare now preserves Workers context when a subrequest targets a Cloudflare-proxied hostname using Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP). These requests are identified as Cloudflare-to-Cloudflare traffic instead of external Internet traffic.

Previously, some BYOIP subrequests could lose Workers context and original client signals. This could cause security rules to behave unexpectedly, Bot Management to evaluate an internal Cloudflare connection instead of the original client, or affected requests to return false 403 responses.

Workers subrequests to BYOIP destinations now preserve the CF-Worker header and cf.worker.upstream_zone field. This supports consistent security rule evaluation across same-zone and cross-zone subrequests.

Bot Management fields on the destination zone now represent the original end-user connection for affected BYOIP subrequests. Bot scores, verified bot status, and JA3/JA4 fingerprints no longer represent the internal connection between Cloudflare services.

Because Cloudflare-proxied BYOIP destinations now follow standard Workers subrequest handling, cross-zone requests set CF-Connecting-IP to the Workers client IP address 2a06:98c0:3600::103 for security reasons. This applies when a Worker in one Cloudflare zone sends a subrequest to a hostname in another Cloudflare zone. Same-zone subrequests continue to reflect the client IP through CF-Connecting-IP.

For more information, refer to Cloudflare BYOIP, Workers subrequests, and CF-Connecting-IP in Worker subrequests.

item.title: Agents - Agents SDK: Agent Skills are files in your agent's Workspace
item.description:
Agent Skills in the Cloudflare Agents SDK are now files. Write a folder with a SKILL.md into your agent's Computer ↗︎ Workspace, under /workspace/.agents/skills/, and the agent can use it on its next turn. You do not need a build step or a deploy, and the agent can write its own skills.

This release includes:

  • Three sources. Load skills from a Computer Workspace, an R2 bucket, or code. Think lists every source again before each turn.
  • The open format. Every SKILL.md is checked against the Agent Skills specification ↗︎. As the specification's guide for agents recommends, a skill that breaks a rule still loads, with a logged warning. Use parseSkill() to check a skill before you write it.
  • Scripts in the Workspace. Skill scripts are Workspace files, and the model runs them with the Workspace exec tool. Refer to Execution.
  • Skill tools for any harness. Use the same activate_skill and read_skill_resource tools in Think, Pi Durable, or the AI SDK. Refer to Skills tools.
  • Warm prompt caches. When a skill changes mid-conversation, Think sends the new catalog as a reminder instead of rebuilding the cached system prompt. An overridden getSystemPrompt() now stays at the top of the system prompt, above context blocks.

This is a breaking change for code that uses agents/skills directly. The agents:skills Vite import, agents/skills/compile, SkillRegistry, and Think's skillWorkspace are removed, and runner() moved to agents/skills/runner. Install Agents SDK v0.32.0 ↗︎ and Think v0.23.0 ↗︎ or later. Refer to the computer-skills ↗︎ and r2-skills ↗︎ examples.

item.title: Data Localization Suite, SSL/TLS - View your data localization settings in one dashboard page
item.description:
The Cloudflare dashboard now includes a Data Localization Suite Overview, a read-only view of the data localization settings on your account. It shows your Regional Services, Customer Metadata Boundary, and Geo Key Manager settings in one place, so you no longer need to check several dashboard pages and APIs to see where your traffic is processed and where your logs and private keys are stored.

To find it, go to Application Security > Data Localization Suite, or search for "DLS" in the dashboard.

The Overview has a tab for each product:

  • Regional Services: regionalized hostnames (filter by region or zone), regionalized IP bindings, and regionalized Spectrum applications, each with its region.
  • Customer Metadata Boundary: whether the boundary is on, the region (US or EU), and whether out-of-region access is allowed.
  • Geo Key Manager: every custom certificate with a geo policy, with its hostname, zone, region, and status.

Each item links to the dashboard page where you change its setting, and each tab links to the product's documentation.

To learn more, refer to the Data Localization Suite documentation.

item.title: Access, Cloudflare One - Google Workspace SCIM user provisioning through generic SAML
item.description:
System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) is an open standard that synchronizes user identities between an identity provider and a service. For more information, refer to SCIM provisioning. Google Workspace is rolling out custom SCIM profiles in beta. Organizations with access to the feature can use Google's built-in provisioning service to send user updates and deprovisioning events to Cloudflare One.

You must use a generic SAML identity provider in Cloudflare One. The dedicated Google Workspace integration does not support SCIM. Configure a SAML app in Google, then enter the Cloudflare SCIM endpoint and secret in the app's autoprovisioning settings. Turn on Enable user deprovisioning in Cloudflare One to revoke active Access sessions when Google deprovisions a user. Google's configured deprovisioning delay still applies. Support for the existing Google Workspace OIDC client will be added once Google adds support for OIDC + SCIM.

Group membership is configured separately. Have the Google SAML app send a groups attribute to include the user's selected Google groups during authentication. Selecting groups as a SCIM provisioning scope does not synchronize group membership, Google is still adding support for this in their SCIM provider.

Cloudflare One users must first authenticate to Access or register a device with the Cloudflare One Client before SCIM updates can apply. Availability of custom SCIM profiles depends on Google's beta rollout.

For setup instructions, refer to Google Workspace (SAML/SCIM).

item.title: Access, Cloudflare One - Filter MCP tool-call analytics by response status
item.description:
MCP tool-call analytics support a response_status query parameter on the account, portal, and server timeseries endpoints. Use success, error, or cached to count one status, or all to include every status.

The default is success. Previously, counts included failed and cached calls. If you need the previous all-status counts, set response_status=all explicitly:

The response includes the selected response_status. Invalid values, including an empty value, return 400.

For all query parameters and scoped endpoints, refer to View tool-call analytics.

item.title: Agents, Browser Run - Agents SDK: Preview dev servers in the browser without public URLs
item.description:
Agents that build websites need to check their work in a real browser. Internal hostnames let your agent's browser preview a dev server running in a container without exposing that server to the public Internet.

With internal hostnames, the persistent browser in the Cloudflare Agents SDK can open sites that only your agent serves. Give the browser hostnames such as preview.internal, and its requests to them go to your agent instead of the Internet. The model can check a dev server in its sandbox, a folder in its workspace, or another Worker in the same browser it uses for the web, and nothing is exposed publicly.

Each internal host has a fetch function that runs in your Durable Object, so it can use the object's bindings and state. A host can also send its requests straight to another Worker through a service binding. Add a target schema to a host, and the model chooses what it serves, such as which port or which folder.

Internal hostnames are a capability of the browser, independent of your agent harness. Use the built-in adapters for Pi Durable, AI SDK, and TanStack AI, or connect another harness by implementing a tool with browser.session(). No prebuilt adapter is required.

This example adds a private dev-server preview to a Pi Durable agent. Start with that guide's packages, bindings, and request handler, and install Agents SDK v0.31.0 ↗︎ or later. The example has three parts:

  • Browser configuration: internalHosts defines how the browser reaches the dev server.
  • Durable Object wiring: Lifecycle and fetchInternalHost() connect the browser to your application.
  • Harness integration: browserTool from agents/browser/pi registers the tool with Pi.

To use another harness, keep the browser configuration. Choose a browser-tool adapter if one is available, or implement a tool using browser.session().

browserTool tells the model about each host, including the schema of its target. Because preview.internal has a target schema, the model can choose which port it serves. To check its dev server, the model calls browser.assignHost() with a target that matches the schema, such as { port: 5173 }, and opens the URL it gets back:

The target is checked against the schema and stored, so it lasts across turns, browser restarts, and redeploys. Each request to http://preview.internal/ then calls the host's fetch function with { port: 5173 }.

This release also simplifies browserTool. It runs the model's code in its own Dynamic Worker and no longer needs a CodemodeRuntime export. Refer to the v0.31.0 upgrade notes ↗︎ if you already use browserTool.

For the complete example, limits, and security guidance, refer to Internal hostnames.

item.title: China Network, Challenges, Bots - China-native Challenge Pages for the China Network
item.description:
Challenge Pages served through the Cloudflare China Network now use Turnstile widgets hosted in Mainland China. This means that visitors in Mainland China can complete challenges faster and more reliably because widgets no longer need to make cross-border requests.

You do not need to take any action: this change applies automatically when a China Network zone presents a Challenge Page. Visitors served by Cloudflare's global network will continue to receive the global Challenge Page experience.

For more information, refer to Interstitial Challenge Pages and Cloudflare China Network.

item.title: WAF - Malicious uploads detection flags non-multipart Content-Type headers with a boundary
item.description:
The malicious uploads detection now sets cf.waf.content_scan.has_failed to true for requests whose Content-Type header has a boundary parameter but type is not multipart/*, for example application/json; boundary=example. The body of these requests is not scanned.

For more information, refer to Multipart requests.

item.title: WAF - WAF Release - 2026-10-28
item.description:
This release introduces updates to the underlying rule expressions for PHP out-of-memory (OOM) vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 ↗︎, CVE-2026-109619 ↗︎ and CVE-2026-115560 ↗︎. The improvements are iterative changes based on reports from Security Researchers as part of PHP Capture the Flag (CTF) challenge ↗︎.

Cloudflare Free RulesetN/APHP Remote Code Execution Attack (CVE-2026-109618 ↗︎, CVE-2026-109619 ↗︎, CVE-2026-115560 ↗︎) #6BlockBlockRule detection updated.

item.title: Workers VPC - Select a virtual network for VPC Network bindings
item.description:
VPC Network bindings can select a specific virtual network by setting network_id to cf1:vnet:<UUID>, where the UUID is the ID of the virtual network. Continue to use cf1:network to select your account's default virtual network.

Multiple bindings can select different virtual networks. This lets one Worker reach separate backends that use the same private IP address:

For details, refer to VPC Networks configuration.

item.title: Workers - Workers Builds now retains builds and build logs for 90 days
item.description:
Workers Builds now retains each build and its build logs for 90 days after the build finishes. You can find them under View build history in your Worker's Deployments tab, or through the Workers Builds API.

After 90 days, a build and its logs are removed. The versions and deployments it created stay in your Worker's version history, so you can still roll back to them.

If you need a build's logs for longer, you can download them with the Get build logs API endpoint.

For more information, refer to the Workers Builds limits documentation.

item.title: Cloudflare One, Access - Fully customize user-facing Access pages
item.description:
Cloudflare Access now supports HTML and Liquid templates for login, identity-denied, forbidden, and command-line approval pages. Custom templates allow you to control the branding and appearance of each supported page. Liquid variables allow you to provide custom instructions to users or provide a clear reason why they were blocked.

Create templates in the Cloudflare One dashboard, validate them in the editor, and assign them to applications or set account defaults.

Custom templates are available on Zero Trust Pay-as-you-go and Enterprise plans. They are not available on the Zero Trust Free plan.

For supported page types, template examples, and setup instructions, refer to Access custom pages.

item.title: Analytics - SQL API introspection: `include_attributes` parameter
item.description:
The SQL API introspection endpoint has a new include_attributes query parameter. Setting it to true discovers the keys of a dataset's attributes JSON column, and their types, from the preceding seven days of your account's data. Discovered keys are returned in the dataset's attributes response field.

Some datasets store additional key-value data in an attributes JSON column, which you query with exact-key lookups such as attributes['http.method']. The previous way to discover these keys, include_custom_attributes, returned names in a custom_attributes field. The new names make it clearer that each returned name is a key you access through the attributes column.

include_custom_attributes and custom_attributes are deprecated but still work. Update integrations to use include_attributes and attributes.

For more information, refer to Attributes.

item.title: Workflows, Workers - Restrict Workflows to a jurisdiction
item.description:
You can now restrict a Workflow to a jurisdiction. Its instances only run and store data within that jurisdiction, which helps you comply with data localization regulations such as GDPR ↗︎ or FedRAMP ↗︎.

Set jurisdiction on a workflows binding, or on a Workflow declared in exports:

The supported jurisdictions are eu (the European Union), us (the United States), and fedramp (FedRAMP-Moderate data centers).

A Workflow's jurisdiction is set when the Workflow is created, and cannot be changed afterwards. If an existing Workflow has a different jurisdiction, wrangler deploy and wrangler versions upload stop before uploading your Worker.

Workflow jurisdictions require Wrangler 4.152.0 or above.

For more information, refer to Data location.

item.title: Agents, Workers - Cloudflare Computer now helps agents recover from interruptions and wait for approval
item.description:
@cloudflare/computer ↗︎ gives your agent a workspace to run code in. From v0.7.0, that code can resume after a deploy or crash, and pause on an external action, for example to approve a tool call.

Resume interrupted runs

Set onInterrupt: "replay" on WorkerJavaScriptBackend, or on a single run.

When recovery is triggered, the JavaScript runs again from the beginning, reusing recorded results for completed calls without printing previously recorded output again. If a call's result was not recorded before the interruption, recovery may repeat the call — even if its action already succeeded. For retry handling, including unsafeToRepeat() for operations that cannot safely repeat, refer to Calls that must not run twice.

Recovery starts on the next call to workspace.runtime. To recover without waiting for traffic, call workspace.runtime.recover() from a Durable Object alarm.

Wait for approvals

Expose your application functions through custom modules. A function can call ctx.interrupt() to pause the run until your application supplies an approval decision.

Require approval before posting a comment

For example, to provide a GitHub module that allows an agent to post a comment on an issue with approval, an implementation of postComment could look like this:

Call it from agent code

When the agent's code calls postComment(), the run pauses at ctx.interrupt() until your app responds. The agent's code calls it like any other function:

Respond to the approval request

The time spent waiting does not count toward its timeout. The wait also survives deploys. Fetch the pending calls with workspace.runtime.pending() and resolve them with respond():

The run continues once all pending calls are resolved.

For setup, current limitations, and how replay works, refer to Resume runs after a restart.

item.title: DNS - Advanced Nameservers use a nameserver type
item.description:
Starting today, the DNS settings endpoints gradually begin to represent Advanced Nameservers with nameservers.type: "cloudflare.advanced". The rollout is expected to take seven days. Previously, the API used the "foundation_dns": true setting for this configuration.

Before the rollout reaches an account, the endpoints continue to return nameservers.type: "cloudflare.standard" for Advanced Nameservers. The endpoints accept nameservers.type: "cloudflare.advanced" in PATCH requests for entitled accounts throughout the rollout. The zone settings JSON for /zones/{zone_id}/dns_settings is:

Cloudflare will make an equivalent change to /accounts/{account_id}/dns_settings at the same time.

The foundation_dns boolean remains available as a deprecated compatibility alias in zone and account-default settings. Use nameservers.type: "cloudflare.advanced" for new writes.

You can continue to read and write foundation_dns during this transition. If a PATCH request includes both values, they must match. The API rejects conflicting values.

Update clients that treat nameservers.type as a closed enum to recognize the "cloudflare.advanced" value.

This API update does not change your Foundation DNS subscription or whether Advanced Nameservers are enabled on your zones. It does not require a zone migration.

In a future API change, Cloudflare will remove the foundation_dns parameter from the API endpoint. After migrating to nameservers.type, remove handling for the boolean from your client.

item.title: Workers - Workers tracing — new spanContext(), setStatus(), and updateName() APIs
item.description:
Custom spans in Workers now support three more methods from the OpenTelemetry span API.

  • span.spanContext() returns the span's traceId, spanId, and traceFlags. The IDs match the trace and span IDs in Workers Observability and in exported traces, so you can log them or return them to clients to correlate a request with its trace.
  • span.setStatus(status) sets the span status to "unset", "ok", or "error", with an optional message for errors. Span status is included in traces exported to OpenTelemetry destinations. The Workers Observability dashboard does not display it yet.
  • span.updateName(name) renames a span after it starts, such as once you know which route a request matched. You can also rename the invocation's root span returned by tracing.getActiveSpan().

For more details, refer to the custom spans documentation.

item.title: WAF - WAF Release - 2026-10-25 - Emergency - Cloudflare Managed Ruleset
item.description:
This emergency release will add two rules related to the Brotli vulnerability CVE-2026-111497 ↗︎ to the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset. Both rules will be enabled by default with their action set to Log, providing visibility into matching requests so customers can evaluate the impact before choosing to block them.

Rule behavior

  • Brotli rule: Matches incoming requests that declare Brotli request-body encoding (Content-Encoding: br), including legitimate clients submitting Brotli-encoded request bodies. It does not match Accept-Encoding: br or affect Cloudflare's Brotli response-compression settings. The rule's default action is Log.
  • Next.js rule: Matches requests to the Next.js image optimization endpoint (/_next/image), including legitimate image optimization traffic. The default action is Log and does not block requests. Changing the action to Block may prevent optimized images from loading and disrupt image delivery for applications using this endpoint.

Default behavior

  • Both rules will log matching requests without blocking them when the ruleset defaults are used.
  • Customers will be able to review matches in analytics and configure a blocking action for either rule if desired.
  • Enabling these rules in Log mode provides visibility only; it does not block requests matching these rules.

Important: Check existing action overrides

If you have configured a ruleset-level action override that applies Block to these rules, matching requests may be blocked as soon as the rules are deployed, despite their default Log action. This may result in false positives and block legitimate traffic.

Review your existing ruleset overrides before deployment. If you want to evaluate these rules without blocking traffic, configure rule-specific overrides to use Log and review matching requests before switching to Block.

Cloudflare Managed RulesetN/ABrotli - Request Content-Encoding - CVE:CVE-2026-111497 ↗︎N/ALogThis is a new detection.

item.title: D1 - D1 database undelete requests limited to the last 7 days
item.description:
The D1 undelete API now only accepts requests for databases that were deleted within the last 7 days. Requests to undelete a database that was deleted more than 7 days ago will fail and return an error.

If you delete a D1 database by mistake, send the undelete request as soon as possible, and no later than 7 days after deletion.

For more information, refer to the undelete D1 database API reference.

item.title: Flagship - Target Flagship feature flags with structured evaluation context
item.description:
Flagship supports nested objects, arrays, and null in evaluation context. Pass user profiles and tag lists directly, then target nested attributes without flattening your application data.

For example, pass a profile and tags when evaluating a flag through the Workers binding:

A targeting rule can combine profile.plan equals "enterprise" with tags has "beta" to serve the feature to enterprise users in the beta group. Use dot-separated paths for nested attributes and the has and not_has operators for array membership. Percentage rollouts can also use a nested identifier, such as profile.id, for consistent user assignment.

Structured context works through the Workers binding, the evaluation REST API with a JSON POST body, and the TypeScript, Python, and Go OpenFeature SDKs from version 0.6.0. The SDKs automatically use POST when HTTP evaluation requires structured context.

Refer to targeting rules, the evaluation API, and SDK context support for usage and supported values.

item.title: Radar - Redesigned Cloudflare Radar homepage
item.description:
The Cloudflare Radar homepage has been redesigned to make global Internet data easier to explore for broader audiences, including journalists, policymakers, and everyday users, while preserving the depth that technical users rely on.

  • Interactive map: Shows Internet traffic and outages around the world, and acts as a starting point for exploring specific countries and trends.
  • Curated insights section: Tabbed navigation that highlights summary statistics across Radar data, with a call to action to explore each area in depth.
  • Updated interface: Built with Kumo ↗︎ components, the same ones used across Cloudflare products.

As we continue the redesign, all Radar pages will see improvements. Share feedback at radar@cloudflare.com.

For more details, read the blog post ↗︎ or visit Cloudflare Radar ↗︎.

item.title: Workers, Pages - Workers Builds and Pages build images reject compromised eMudhra certificates
item.description:
The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities ↗︎ can be recovered, so anyone can forge a certificate for any hostname that chains to them. The Workers Builds and Pages build images now reject these certificates when your build clones your repository, installs dependencies, or makes HTTPS requests.

The updated images include patched CA certificates, Node.js 22.23.4 and 24.22.1, Bun 1.4.4, and pip 26.2.2. Build commands also run with environment variables that point older runtimes at the patched CA certificates.

What you need to do

Most projects need no changes. Update your project if:

  • You set BUN_VERSION below 1.4.4. Older Bun versions trust the compromised certificates.
  • You set your own SSL_CERT_FILE, PIP_CERT, or REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, or set --use-bundled-ca in NODE_OPTIONS. Make sure your CA certificates do not trust the compromised intermediates.
  • Your build installs tools that ship their own CA certificates. Update them to a version that removes the compromised intermediates.

For details, refer to the build image documentation for Workers Builds and Pages.

item.title: Workers - Pin your npm version in Workers Builds with packageManager
item.description:
You can now choose the npm version that Workers Builds uses by setting the packageManager field in your package.json. Before the build installs dependencies, it installs the npm version you set, so a lockfile written by a newer npm version installs the same way in your build as it does locally.

The packageManager field also sets the version of Yarn, pnpm, and Bun. Use an exact version, such as npm@11.19.1, not a range. Workers Builds does not use the engines.npm field to choose an npm version.

For more information, refer to Package manager versions.

item.title: Cloudflare One Client - Cloudflare One Client for Windows (version 2026.9.1555.1)
item.description:
A new Beta release for the Windows Cloudflare One Client is now available on the beta releases downloads page.

This release includes the following highlights:

  • Added automatic endpoint selection for Global Acceleration. When Global Acceleration is enabled for an organization, the client connects to the Global Acceleration endpoints while the device is in the acceleration region and to the standard anycast endpoints otherwise, and reconnects when a network change moves the device between them without requiring action from the user. The Connectivity page shows which tunnel and API endpoints are in use, and users who are allowed to override the selection can choose endpoints in Settings.
  • Added protection against unauthorized modification or uninstallation of the Cloudflare One Client. When enabled, the user will be asked to provide an administrator-generated code when trying to uninstall the client, which will otherwise be blocked.
  • The client now shows a banner when the network limits the tunnel MTU to a degraded or critically low value. The banner clears when the MTU recovers or the client disconnects.

Additional Changes and improvements

  • The client now applies tunnel MTUs between 1147 and 1199 bytes measured by Path MTU Discovery. Previously the client ignored these values and kept a larger MTU, which could drop larger packets on networks such as mobile hotspots while the client showed as connected.
  • When Path MTU Discovery is enabled, the client now accepts larger packets from Cloudflare instead of limiting them to the size it uses for its own outbound packets.
  • Access reauthentication requests now trust certificates in the operating system's certificate store, so reauthentication works on networks that perform TLS inspection.
  • For Zero Trust deployments, the client now records a traceroute of the network path outside the tunnel when the tunnel degrades or fails to connect. warp-diag includes the same trace.
  • warp-diag now includes redacted copies of the deployed MDM files and the names, but not the values, of stored registration secrets. It reports a QUIC path MTU only when one was measured.
  • Added the MDM parameters mdm_file_debounce_secs (1–60) and mdm_file_unavailable_debounce_secs (0–300), which set how long the client waits before applying a changed MDM file and before acting on a missing or unreadable one.
  • The consumer client home screen now shows when the connection is post-quantum encrypted.
  • The client UI no longer starts WMIC or PowerShell processes to collect memory information for crash reports.
  • Fixed a hostname-based split tunnel entry not taking effect until the next reconnect after its firewall rule failed to apply.
  • Fixed the client window appearing blank or white after an upgrade, at sign-in, after waking from sleep, or after a display change.
  • Fixed the client service restarting when a firewall update for captive portal detection stalled while the device was asleep.
  • Fixed the client getting stuck in a disconnected state on Windows on Arm devices because leftover tunnel adapters were not removed.
  • Fixed the client being unable to connect after an upgrade, downgrade, and upgrade that switched between consumer and Zero Trust registrations. The client now clears the mismatched registration so the user can register again.
  • Fixed the client UI looking for one of its libraries in a directory that standard users can create before looking in the installation directory.
  • Fixed warp-cli registration license reporting an error on slow networks even though the license was applied, which left the client registered to a WARP+ account it did not recognize.
  • Fixed Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX) results being reported with timestamps offset from the actual time after the system clock was corrected.
  • Added the MDM parameters managed_network_probe_interval_secs (30–300, default 30) and managed_network_probe_count (0 disables probing, 1–10, or -1 to keep probing until a managed network is found; default 1). After a registration or network change finds no managed network, the client now rechecks, so a device doesn't stay on the default profile because of a transient connection failure. Set the count to 0 to keep the previous behavior.
  • In proxy mode for Zero Trust, the client now sends hostnames from HTTP/HTTPS and SOCKS5 requests to Cloudflare for resolution instead of resolving them on the device.
  • When the app cannot reach the client service, the home screen now says why (service not running, not accepting connections, not responding, or connection dropped and reconnecting). It shows an error code and a Learn more link instead of "IPC error".
  • Fixed Windows resetting the Wi-Fi adapter after sign-in or a Wi-Fi restart when the client's firewall rules in Exclude split tunnel mode blocked Windows network connectivity checks. The client now allows those checks.
  • Fixed the installer asking the user to close running applications during an upgrade, downgrade or uninstall because other programs loaded the client's Visual C++ runtime libraries through the system PATH. The client now loads these libraries from a private folder so that closing other applications is unnecessary.

Known issues

A Windows DNS client regression may cause connectivity check failures on systems containing large hosts files. While our client includes a mitigation for this issue, users may still experience reduced DNS performance and connectivity check failures.

For Zero Trust documentation please see: https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/ For Consumer documentation please see: https://developers.cloudflare.com/warp-client/

item.title: Cloudflare One Client - Cloudflare One Client for macOS (version 2026.9.1555.1)
item.description:
A new Beta release for the macOS Cloudflare One Client is now available on the beta releases downloads page.

This release includes the following highlights:

  • macOS 15.0 is now the minimum supported version. This release does not run on macOS 14.
  • Added automatic endpoint selection for Global Acceleration. When Global Acceleration is enabled for an organization, the client connects to the Global Acceleration endpoints while the device is in the acceleration region and to the standard anycast endpoints otherwise, and reconnects when a network change moves the device between them without requiring action from the user.. The Connectivity page shows which tunnel and API endpoints are in use, and users who are allowed to override the selection can choose endpoints in Settings.
  • The client now shows a banner when the network limits the tunnel MTU to a degraded or critically low value. The banner clears when the MTU recovers or the client disconnects.

Additional Changes and improvements

  • The client now applies tunnel MTUs between 1147 and 1199 bytes measured by Path MTU Discovery. Previously the client ignored these values and kept a larger MTU, which could drop larger packets on networks such as mobile hotspots while the client showed as connected.
  • When Path MTU Discovery is enabled, the client now accepts larger packets from Cloudflare instead of limiting them to the size it uses for its own outbound packets.
  • Access reauthentication requests now trust certificates in the operating system's certificate store, so reauthentication works on networks that perform TLS inspection.
  • For Zero Trust deployments, the client now records a traceroute of the network path outside the tunnel when the tunnel degrades or fails to connect. warp-diag includes the same trace.
  • warp-diag now includes redacted copies of the deployed MDM files and reports a QUIC path MTU only when one was measured.
  • The consumer client home screen now shows when the connection is post-quantum encrypted.
  • Fixed a managed registration being removed when the MDM configuration file was briefly missing or unreadable. The client now keeps the last applied policy for 20 seconds after the file becomes unavailable. The new MDM parameters mdm_file_debounce_secs (1–60) and mdm_file_unavailable_debounce_secs (0–300) change how long the client waits before applying a changed file and before acting on a missing one.
  • Fixed a hostname-based split tunnel entry not taking effect until the next reconnect after its firewall rule failed to apply.
  • Fixed split tunnel updates for hostname-based entries failing when the client tried to remove a route that macOS had not installed.
  • Fixed the client UI not showing onboarding on first launch while a notification permission request was pending.
  • Fixed warp-cli registration license reporting an error on slow networks even though the license was applied, which left the client registered to a WARP+ account it did not recognize.
  • Fixed Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX) results being reported with timestamps offset from the actual time after the system clock was corrected.
  • Fixed an upgrade sometimes leaving the client without a running service when the previous service was slow to stop. The installer now waits up to 10 seconds for the old service to be removed before starting the new one.
  • Fixed the OS version detail stored for a device keeping an outdated value, including the text "Usage: sw_vers…" reported by client versions 2023.5.587.1 through 2024.12.760.0. The client now clears the value the next time it connects.
  • Added the MDM parameters managed_network_probe_interval_secs (30–300, default 30) and managed_network_probe_count (0 disables probing, 1–10, or -1 to keep probing until a managed network is found; default 1). After a registration or network change finds no managed network, the client now rechecks, so a device doesn't stay on the default profile because of a transient connection failure. Set the count to 0 to keep the previous behavior.
  • In proxy mode for Zero Trust, the client now sends hostnames from HTTP/HTTPS and SOCKS5 requests to Cloudflare for resolution, instead of resolving them on the device.
  • When the app cannot reach the client service, the home screen now says why (service not running, not accepting connections, not responding, or connection dropped and reconnecting). It shows an error code and a Learn more link instead of "IPC error".

Known issues

None.

For Zero Trust documentation please see: https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/ For Consumer documentation please see: https://developers.cloudflare.com/warp-client/

item.title: Agents - Cloudflare MCP servers no longer serve /sse
item.description:
Cloudflare's product-specific MCP servers now serve only /mcp. A request to /sse returns 410 Gone with the server's /mcp URL, which most MCP clients show in their connection error.

If your MCP client is configured with an /sse URL, change it to /mcp, for example https://docs.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp. If you signed in through /sse, your client asks you to sign in again. Connections that already use /mcp are not affected.

item.title: Agents - Agents SDK now supports the latest Pi 1.4 release
item.description:
Agents SDK v0.30.0 runs PiHarness on Pi 1.4 ↗︎, and makes it recover more reliably from evictions, crashes, and storage errors.

  • Hibernation while Pi's tasks sleep. PiHarness passes Pi's new onWake callback to your harness factory. While a task sleeps, such as during a model retry backoff, the Durable Object can hibernate until the task is due instead of staying in memory.
  • Parked tasks. Pi 1.4 parks a task that keeps crashing the object instead of restarting it forever. Parked operations show as parked in pending(), and session.retry() runs them again.
  • Recovery from storage errors. PiHarness reopens Pi after a storage error instead of failing every call until the object restarts. Its wake-up job retries failed steps with a backoff instead of being dropped.
  • Retried model streams. agents/models/pi-ai reports a cut-off or idle model stream as a transient error, so Pi retries the turn instead of failing it.

Upgrade

The Agents SDK v0.30.0 changelog ↗︎ has step-by-step upgrade instructions. Point your coding agent at them and upgrade today:

Pi 1.4 migrates the session storage in the object's SQLite database to a schema that Pi 1.3 cannot open, so a deployment cannot roll back past this upgrade. Refer to the Pi Durable 1.4.0 changelog ↗︎ for Pi's own breaking changes.

item.title: Sandboxes - Sandbox SDK 0.12.14 updates trusted certificates after the eMudhra compromise
item.description:
The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities ↗︎ can be recovered, so anyone can forge a certificate for any hostname that chains to them. Sandbox SDK images before 0.12.14 trust these certificates. An HTTPS connection that leaves the container directly, such as one from mountBucket(), backups, gitCheckout(), tunnels, or code that runs in the sandbox, can be intercepted with a forged certificate.

What you need to do

Sandbox SDK 0.x

Update immediately. Install @cloudflare/sandbox@0.12.14, change the FROM line in your Dockerfile to the matching image, and redeploy. Keep any -python, -opencode, or -musl suffix on the image tag. The deployment's rollout replaces running sandboxes with ones that use the new image.

If you use the next prerelease, update to 0.13.0-next.825.1 or later.

If you cannot update yet and use 0.8.7 or later, send all HTTPS through your Worker, so that Cloudflare checks every certificate on port 443 whatever your image trusts:

Deploy, then stop running sandboxes so that they restart with the interception certificate. This does not cover TLS on other ports, such as cloudflared tunnels, and clients that ignore the injected certificate fail to connect. For more information, refer to HTTPS traffic.

Sandbox SDK 1.x

You do not need to update the SDK, because it makes no TLS connections of its own. Your image decides which certificates your sandboxes trust, so rebuild it and replace the sandboxes that run the old one:

  1. Run docker pull for each base image in your Dockerfile, then clear the Docker build cache with docker builder prune --all. wrangler deploy builds with your local images and build cache, so without these steps it can ship the old CA certificates and runtimes. If your Wrangler configuration references an image by digest, build and push a new image and update the digest instead.
  2. Deploy your Worker.
  3. Stop sandboxes that are still running, for example with this.ctx.container.destroy(). A running sandbox keeps the image it started with until it stops. To restart only the sandboxes whose image is out of date, refer to Roll out a named image update.
  4. If you use snapshots, create new ones from sandboxes that run the updated image. A snapshot restores the image it was created from, so an older snapshot brings back the old certificates.

Check your sandboxes

From inside a sandbox, connect to one of the test hosts listed at emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com ↗︎ with each TLS client your code uses, such as curl, node, or bun. Every request should fail:

What changed in 0.12.13 and 0.12.14

In the 0.12.13 images, the system CA bundle, Node.js, cloudflared, and pip reject certificates from the compromised intermediates. The images ship updated Ubuntu and Alpine CA certificates, Node.js 22.23.4, cloudflared 2026.10.2, and pip 26.2.2 in the -python image.

0.12.14 updates Bun to 1.4.4, so the bun command and createBackup() uploads of archives of 10 MiB or more reject these certificates too. The -opencode image ships OpenCode 1.19.4 or later, which also runs on Bun 1.4.4.

item.title: Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare Tunnel for SASE - Cloudflare Tunnel supports URL normalization
item.description:
Starting from version 2026.10.0, Cloudflare Tunnel can normalize URLs before matching ingress rules. This improves security for tunnels with rules that require Cloudflare Access validation. The URL path sent to your origin stays the same.

In three months, starting 2027-01-25, new cloudflared releases will turn on URL normalization by default. Test your path-based routing before that date, as this change may affect which ingress rule matches a request. Configurations without rules requiring Access validation are unaffected.

This setting is currently off by default. To turn it on, run:

Alternatively, set TUNNEL_DISABLE_PATH_NORMALIZATION=false on each cloudflared replica and restart it.

For more information, refer to ingress matching and Access validation at the origin.

item.title: Cloudflare Fundamentals, Cloudflare One, Cloudflare Tunnel for SASE, Cloudflare Tunnel - Granular Tunnel Read And Monitor role is generally available
item.description:
The Cloudflare Tunnel - Granular Connector cloudflared Read And Monitor role is now generally available. You can grant a member read access and log streaming for specific Cloudflare Tunnel instances without granting write access or access to every Tunnel in your account.

This role includes the same access as Cloudflare Tunnel - Granular Connector cloudflared Read: viewing selected Tunnels, their IP and hostname routes, and connector host details. It also grants remote log streaming, so support operators can troubleshoot a Tunnel without changing its configuration. The existing Read role does not grant log streaming access.

To assign the role, follow Grant a granular permission. For the available roles, refer to the resource-scoped roles reference.

item.title: Agents, Workers AI, AI Gateway - createAI replaces workers-ai-provider and ai-gateway-provider
item.description:
The Agents SDK has a new createAI function for the AI SDK and Pi AI. It unifies what workers-ai-provider and ai-gateway-provider did: Workers AI models, AI Gateway catalog models, dynamic routes, and vendor models, through the AI binding or an account id and API token.

workers-ai-provider and ai-gateway-provider are now feature frozen and marked as deprecated. Please migrate at your convenience.

With createAI you get:

  • Every model by id. Workers AI @cf/ ids, any model in the AI Gateway catalog, and dynamic routes as dynamic/<route>.
  • Vendor model objects. Pass a model from the vendor's own package, such as ai(anthropic("claude-opus-5-5")). It goes unchanged to AI Gateway's provider-native endpoint.
  • The binding, or an account id and API token. Use a gateway in another account, or call from outside a Worker.
  • Gateway options, fallback, and BYOK. Caching, logging, metadata, retries, byokAlias, zdr, and vendorKey.
  • Stream resume. Through the binding, a catalog or dynamic route stream that drops mid-answer resumes.
  • Other model types. Embeddings, images, speech, transcription, and reranking in the AI SDK provider, and images in Pi AI.
Before After
createWorkersAI({ binding }) createAI({ binding })
createWorkersAI({ accountId, apiKey }) createAI({ accountId, apiToken })
createAiGateway(...) createAI(...), with fallback for a list of models
createAISearch from workers-ai-provider createAISearchNamespace from ai-search-provider

For AI Search, use ai-search-provider. For more information, refer to Models.

item.title: Basin SQL, Basin - Basin SQL supports OFFSET
item.description:
Basin SQL is a serverless, distributed SQL engine for querying Apache Iceberg tables in Basin Catalog. It now supports OFFSET, which lets you skip a specified number of rows when retrieving query results.

Use LIMIT to set the page size and OFFSET to skip earlier rows. With a page size of 100, use OFFSET 0 for the first page, OFFSET 100 for the second, and increase the offset by 100 for each later page. Add ORDER BY on a unique column to keep the row order consistent.

For example, this query returns the second page of 100 rows:

For syntax and examples, refer to the OFFSET clause in the Basin SQL reference.

item.title: logpush, Logs - Account-scoped HTTP request logs in Logpush
item.description:
Cloudflare Logpush now supports HTTP request logs as an account-scoped dataset. Use one job to deliver logs for every zone in an account instead of maintaining a separate job for each zone.

Create the job at the account level in the Cloudflare dashboard or through the Logpush API. The ZoneName field identifies the source zone in each log entry.

Custom fields remain configured per zone. An account-scoped job honors the custom fields configuration for each zone but does not support account-wide custom fields configuration.

For setup details, refer to API configuration.

item.title: WAF - Response custom rules
item.description:
The response firewall can block responses before they reach visitors. Cloudflare turns on default protections for everyone, on every plan.

Every plan includes three response custom rules per zone. These rules run in the http_response_firewall_custom phase.

Rules support the block, log, and execute actions. You can include at most one execute rule within the three-rule allowance.

Response custom rules can combine request fields with response fields. For requests to /api/ paths, this expression matches responses with status code 500:

For background, refer to the full transaction detection announcement ↗︎.

For supported actions, fields, and limits, refer to Response firewall.
